subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Expectations as Reference Points
description: One-minute skill: Expectations as Reference Points.

hook.text: A restaurant with five stars on Yelp disappoints. A diner with two stars delights. Expectations set the bar.

buildup.text: Koszegi and Rabin argued that our reference point is whatever we recently expected to happen.

discovery.text: Expectations form a mental anchor. Every outcome is judged as better or worse than what we anticipated.

twist.text: Under-promise and over-deliver works because it sets a low reference point. Anything above it feels like a win.

climax.text: Managing others' expectations is managing their reference points. Lower the bar and then clear it.

punchline.text: Set expectations low. Then exceed them.

quiz.question: Why does under-promising and over-delivering work?
options: It sets a low reference point, making the outcome feel like a gain
